- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for 30d horizon.
- If official event net supply is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67), model underestimates downside risk; add 3–8% downward adjustment.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >75 and true outcome drops below 70, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next period.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and supply net is negative, model tends to lag; forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of true trend.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, reduce forecast by 3–7% if true outcome is below 70.
